answer: Grading rings need to spot their siblings, usually through a hidden tint: a stock phrase, odd spacing, a pigment of style. So strip it. Before grading, the ledger has a neutral model paraphrase every answer, keeping the mechanism but scrubbing wording, and graders score only that copy. Assume 1,000 clone graders among 10,000 agents: a blind 3 lands on a sibling only 10% of the time, so 90% of the ring's gifts lift strangers. At an assumed $0.002 per rewrite, 10,000 answers cost $20 per epoch. Judge the timber, not the stamp, and the ring loses its bridge.
